subject.title: iOS app: push notifications for assistant messages + background Talk mode

question: Should native iOS assistant-message notifications use generic APNs alerts by default, allow transcript previews behind explicit opt-in, or stay unsupported until a broader mobile notification privacy model is approved?
rationale: The APNs registration, relay, local notification, and exec-approval push pieces exist, but payload content, lock-screen privacy, tap routing, duplicate-foreground behavior, and per-device opt-in semantics require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Approve Generic Chat Alerts
options.body: Add a dedicated chat-reply APNs kind and iOS tap route with generic notification content by default, leaving transcript previews for a later explicit opt-in.

options.title: Allow Opt-In Previews
options.body: Permit assistant reply text in APNs only behind a visible per-device or per-gateway privacy setting with tests and docs for lock-screen behavior.

options.title: Defer Native Chat Pushes
options.body: Keep relying on foreground app state and third-party channels until maintainers define a broader mobile notification policy.

recommendation.title: Approve Generic Chat Alerts
recommendation.body: Add a dedicated chat-reply APNs kind and iOS tap route with generic notification content by default, leaving transcript previews for a later explicit opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available product-surface routing candidate from the iOS Talk/chat history, while APNs implementation details likely need input from ngutman.
